Subject: POC acceptance criteria, evaluation plan, and capacity safeguards

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment on scope. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed acceptance criteria for the 3-week POC and the capacity guardrails we'll put in place so you can evaluate performance under realistic load. Attaching a short playbook and a capacity estimate.

POC snapshot (3 weeks)
- Objective: Validate end-to-end latency and cost at 95th percentile for the customer-facing search workflow (batch size: 1, max seq len: 1024).
- Success metrics:
  - 95th percentile generation latency <= 420ms (95% of queries)
  - Mean token cost within 12% of our lab estimate
  - No production-impacting errors during 48-hour soak at target throughput
- Evaluation tests: synthetic replay (30k queries/day), live shadowing of a 5% user sample, quality spot checks against the provided prompt set.

Capacity plan (high level)
- Reserved baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for the POC window (handles steady-state + small bursts).
- Autoscaling: enabled with warm-standby pool and linear scale up to 8 GPUs for sustained bursts; burst throttle to protect downstream services.
- KV/prefix cache: enabled to reduce repeated prompt cost for the search prompt families.

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) reserve the baseline capacity for the trial week starting 2026-06-01.
2) Luminate confirms the prompt set and the three acceptance prompts by EOD Friday 2026-05-14.
3) We run a dry-run replay 48 hours before cutover and share flame/latency traces.

Attachments: redwood_poc_playbook_v1.pdf (overview + test plan), capacity_estimate.xlsx (cost + GPU allocation).

If that all looks good, I can loop in Ben and Aditya to lock the reservation and booking.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — this is very helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:
- For the 95th pct latency target: is the 420ms measured from request receipt to first token or to final token? We typically measure to first token.
- Can you confirm expected cold-start behavior (0 -> 4 GPUs) for the first 10 minutes of a spike? We need to ensure our front-end doesn't start shedding traffic.
- On autoscaling: what is the scale-up step and expected time per step? We want to ensure the 5% shadowing won't introduce user-visible lag.

Acceptance prompts: we'll share the three canonical prompts by 2026-05-14 and Priya will upload the test prompt set to the doc link you shared.

Appreciate the attachments — will review and revert.

Alex

Ben / Aditya — looping you in to request a short reserve for Luminate (deal RDW-3421). Key asks from the call: baseline reserve of 4 A100-eq GPUs from 2026-06-01 for a 3-week window, warm-standby to allow scale to 8 GPUs if needed, and a 48-hour dry-run on 2026-05-30.

Requirements & risks:
- Traffic pattern: replayed historic search queries (steady 15 qps, 5% live shadowing spike to 30 qps), short generation lengths typical for search (mean 80 tokens).
- Soft SLOs: 95th pct <= 420ms (first token preferred per Alex).
- Risk: if autoscaling is slow, we might see user-visible delays during a sustained spike. Would prefer pre-warm if viable.

Can you confirm:
1) We can lock baseline (4 GPUs) and add warm-standby to reach 8 with <90s scale-up per step.
2) Any special kernel/quantization we should pick for this model family to meet the latency target.
3) Cost delta if they request a hard SLA for the trial vs standard POC terms.

Camila — can you be on the dry-run to validate request traces and gather latency traces?

Thanks,
Evelyn

Subject: Re: Fwd: POC acceptance criteria, evaluation plan, and capacity safeguards

All — quick ops commitment. We can provision the baseline 4 A100-eq GPUs for the POC window and configure warm-standby autoscaling up to 8 GPUs. Notes:
- Scale path: 4 -> 6 -> 8 (two-step incremental scale). Each step can complete in ~60-75s if warm-standby nodes are kept initialized (we should enable pre-warm).
- Cold start (0 -> baseline): ~3.5 minutes; we will avoid that path during the POC by scheduling the baseline reservation before cutover.
- Kernel/quant: For the model family you described, use the int8-optimized runtime we validated in our lab; that preserves quality and lowers per-token latency for the 95th pct.
- Cost: baseline-reserve + warm-standby adds an estimated incremental $6k/week over standard on-demand behavior (see capacity_estimate.xlsx). If Luminate wants a formal SLA, add a 15% premium to cover reserved capacity and higher-ops guardrails.

Camila — Evelyn asked you to attend the 48h dry-run on 2026-05-30. Can you confirm availability?

Ben
